ex.en: Shadows get longer when the sun sets.
The kid is playing, stepping on his own shadow.
My shadow showed up in the photo.

note: 귀에 거슬리다 = grating to the ear.

ex.s: 옆 사람 전화 소리가 좀 거슬려요.
ex.en: The phone noise from the person next to me bothers me.
That tone of voice kept bugging me.
This shirt's tag is irritating my neck.

note: A direct boss is usually addressed by title, e.g., 팀장님.

ex.en: My boss is in a bad mood today.
I asked my boss for time off.
What's your new boss like?

note: 위로하다 = to comfort. Don't confuse with 위로 = upward (위 + 로).

ex.en: My friend's words were a big comfort.
Thanks for comforting me.
Music comforts me when things are hard.

note: Similar to 대충 or 약.

ex.en: It takes roughly an hour to the airport.
About how many people are coming?
Roughly how much is the repair?

note: Passive of 끊다. 버스가 끊기다 = the buses stop running.

ex.en: The call suddenly dropped.
The internet keeps cutting out in the tunnel.
The buses stop running at midnight.

note: 채용하다 = to hire. 채용 공고 = job posting.

ex.en: That company is hiring these days.
I applied after seeing the job posting.
I heard there's no entry-level hiring this year.

note: 뽀뽀하다 = a light kiss or peck, e.g., with kids.

ex.en: The two of them kissed in the movie.
The groom kissed the bride at the wedding.
They kissed and said goodbye at the airport.

note: 이혼하다 = to get divorced.

ex.en: That couple divorced last year.
My parents divorced when I was young.
She's lived alone since the divorce.
Want ice cream for dessert?
I bought ice cream at the convenience store.
It was so hot that the ice cream all melted.

note: 핸드크림 = hand cream.

ex.en: Shall I put cream in your coffee?
There's too much cream on the cake.
My hands were dry, so I put on cream.

en: being in charge; person in charge
note: 담당자 = person in charge. 담당하다 = to be responsible for.

ex.en: Who's in charge of this?
I have a new doctor in charge of my care.
Could you put the person in charge on, please?

note: 개봉하다 = to be released / to open.

ex.en: When does that movie come out?
Did you see the movie that came out this week?
Refrigerate after opening.
I like romance movies.
I'm hooked on a romance drama these days.
I heard she found romance on her trip.

note: 그렇게 해요 = let's do that.

ex.en: Let's do that.
Why were you so late?
It's not that cold today.
I finally found the keys I'd lost.
We found the cause of the problem.
I found a hidden gem of a restaurant in my neighborhood.

note: 입학하다 = to start/enter a school. Opposite: 졸업 (graduation).

ex.en: My daughter starts elementary school next year.
Congratulations on getting into school!
When is the entrance ceremony?
There are almost no passengers on the bus.
Passengers, please fasten your seatbelts.
The taxi driver was really kind to the passenger.

note: For thin people use 마르다 or 날씬하다. Pronounced [얄따].

ex.en: This jacket is too thin.
Please slice the meat thin.

ex.s: 벽이 얇아서 옆집 소리가 다 들려요.
ex.en: The walls are thin, so I can hear everything next door.

en: to fly away; be blown or wiped away

ex.en: A bird flew out the window.
My hat blew away in the wind.
The computer shut off and all my files were lost.
I feel a bit down because it's raining.
Why do you look so down lately?
When I feel down, I meet up with friends.
That's not fair.
The referee made fair calls.
Let's split the housework fairly.
Yesterday's traffic was really awful.
Just thinking about it is horrible.
That restaurant's service was terrible.

note: 택시 요금 = taxi fare; 전기 요금 = electric bill.

ex.en: How much was the taxi fare?

ex.s: 이번 달 전기 요금이 많이 나왔어요.
ex.en: This month's electric bill was high.
I changed my phone plan.

note: In school, 국어 = Korean class. The language in general is 한국어.

ex.s: 저는 학교 다닐 때 국어를 제일 좋아했어요.
ex.en: Korean was my favorite class in school.
I have a Korean test tomorrow.
My younger brother is doing his Korean homework.

note: Opposite: 진짜 (real).

ex.en: This bag looks fake.
That's fake news.
A fake smile is easy to spot.

note: Used from the teacher's side; the teacher is 스승.

ex.en: The teacher ran into a former student.
I'm Professor Kim's student.
The students gave their teacher flowers.

note: Counter for words: 한마디 = a word, 몇 마디 = a few words.

ex.en: Let me just say one thing.
I can only speak a few words of English.
My finger joints hurt.

note: 일기를 쓰다 = keep a diary. 일기 예보 (weather forecast) is a different word.

ex.en: I write in my diary every night.
I kept a journal during the trip.
My sister secretly read my diary.
There are lots of shops on both sides of the street.
Both of my ears hurt.
Both sets of parents approved of the marriage.

note: 글씨를 잘 쓰다 = to have nice handwriting.

ex.en: The letters are too small to read.

ex.s: 민호 씨는 글씨를 정말 잘 써요.
ex.en: Minho has really nice handwriting.

ex.s: 칠판 글씨 좀 크게 써 주세요.
ex.en: Please write bigger on the board.
I fell and broke a bone.
Watch out for fish bones.
Milk is good for your bones.
This café's interior is unusual.
What an unusual name.
That friend has a bit of a quirky personality.
That potted plant survived the winter.
It's hard to survive at this company.
I barely survived exam week.

en: to suffer from, be plagued by
note: Takes 에: 두통에 시달리다 = suffer from headaches.

ex.en: I've been suffering from insomnia lately.
I'm exhausted from being swamped with work.
Mosquitoes tormented me all night.

note: Passive of 정리하다.

ex.en: The room is neatly organized now.
Talking it through helped sort out my thoughts.
The documents aren't organized yet.

ex.s: 지우 씨는 병을 극복하고 다시 일해요.
ex.en: Ji-woo overcame her illness and is back at work.
Overcoming fear isn't easy.
I finally got over my slump.
We drove along the coast.
The coastal road is really pretty.
Have you ever been to Korea's east coast?

en: great restaurant, popular place to eat
note: Casual. 맛집 투어 = food tour.

ex.en: Is there a good place to eat around here?
They say this place is a famous spot to eat.
This weekend my friend and I went around to good restaurants.

note: Medical: 검사를 받다 = to get tested.

ex.en: I had my eyes checked at the hospital.
The teacher checked our homework.
I checked the tires before leaving.

note: Hair on your head is 머리카락 or 머리.

ex.en: There's a lot of cat hair on the sofa.
This puppy's fur is really soft.
I shaved my legs.

note: Body temperature is 체온; 온도 = temperature in general.

ex.en: What's the temperature today?
The temperature drops a lot at night.
They say it'll reach 30°C tomorrow.

en: to be compared; to stand out by contrast

ex.en: I hate always being compared to my older sister.

ex.s: 두 폰을 같이 보니까 확 비교돼요.
ex.en: Side by side, the difference between the two phones really shows.
Next to my neighbor's drawing, mine was embarrassing.

note: Mother's brother is 외삼촌. Kids also call friendly men 삼촌.

ex.en: My uncle bought me a present.
We're going to my uncle's place this weekend.
My uncle isn't married yet.
The main character of that movie escapes from prison.

ex.s: 이 사무실은 창문이 없어서 감옥 같아요.
ex.en: This office has no windows, so it feels like a prison.
I had a dream that I went to jail.

note: Honorific form of 그 사람.

ex.en: Who is that person?
He's my senior from college.
Please give her my regards.
There was a home run in the ninth inning.
Our son hit his first home run.

ex.s: 오늘 경기에서 홈런 몇 개 나왔어요?
ex.en: How many home runs were there in today's game?

note: Spoken short form of 아니요.

ex.en: No, I'm fine.
No, this is my first time here.
Coffee? No, tea please.

note: 골프를 치다 = to play golf.

ex.en: My dad plays golf every weekend.
How long have you been learning golf?
It's my first time golfing, so it's really hard.

ex.s: 충전 케이블 좀 빌려줄 수 있어요?
ex.en: Can I borrow your charging cable?
The cable's too short to reach the outlet.
The cable TV isn't working at home.

note: Someone who joined after you. Opposite: 선배 (senior).

ex.en: I had lunch with a junior colleague.
He was a few years behind me in college.
A junior of mine opened up to me about a worry.
It doesn't fit, so I'd like to exchange it.
Let's exchange contact info.
I exchanged gifts with my friends.

note: 주사를 맞다 = to get a shot.

ex.en: I got a shot at the hospital.
The kid is scared of shots.
Did you get a flu shot?

note: Usually with a negative: 절대로 안 돼요 = absolutely not.

ex.en: I'll never forget.

ex.s: 그 비밀은 절대로 말하면 안 돼요.
ex.en: You must never tell that secret.
Never smoke here.

ex.s: 이번 주 토요일에 친구 결혼식이 있어요.
ex.en: My friend's wedding is this Saturday.
What are you wearing to the wedding?
I want a small wedding.
What's your favorite subject?
I'm taking five classes this semester.
Math is my worst subject.
This TV is 55 inches.
The pants have a 32-inch waist.
How many inches is your laptop screen?

note: 초 = the candle itself.

ex.en: Make a wish and blow out the candles!
The power went out, so we lit candles.
We had dinner by candlelight.

note: 현지인 = a local. 현지 시간 = local time.

ex.en: I want to try the local food.

ex.s: 현지 시간으로 오후 세 시에 도착해요.
ex.en: We arrive at 3 p.m. local time.
I asked a local for directions.
The water is really clear.
Please give it to me in a clear cup.
The packaging is clear, so you can see inside.

note: A bit formal; everyday: 허락하다 or -아/어도 돼요.

ex.en: This hotel allows pets.

ex.s: 수업 중에는 휴대폰 사용을 허용하지 않아요.
ex.en: Phones aren't allowed during class.
My company let us work from home.

note: 경찰에 신고하다 = to report to the police.

ex.en: I lost my wallet, so I reported it to the police.
The neighbors were so loud that I reported them.
I have to report my income for taxes.
That teacher is full of passion.
Your passion for cooking is amazing.
My initial enthusiasm has cooled a lot.

note: 기름을 넣다 = to get gas. 기름지다 = greasy.

ex.en: Put a little oil in the pan.
I got oil on my clothes.

ex.s: 가는 길에 기름 좀 넣어야 돼요.
ex.en: I need to get gas on the way.

note: 솔로 is also common for 'single.'

ex.en: I'm still single.
My friend is single, so I set her up on a blind date.

ex.s: 싱글 침대 두 개 있는 방 있어요?
ex.en: Do you have a room with two single beds?

note: 난리가 나다 = all hell breaks loose.

ex.en: The house is a mess because of the kids.
It was the first day of the sale, so the store was chaos.
I lost my phone and it was total panic.

note: Two different words: 화상 (burn) and 화상 (video), as in 화상 통화.

ex.en: I got burned by hot water.
Cool a burn with cold water.
Let's have the meeting by video call later.
Someone's knocking on the door.
Can you pat my back?
I tapped the watermelons to pick one.

note: Konglish: 노트 = notebook, but 노트북 = laptop.

ex.en: I took notes in my notebook.
Can you lend me a notebook?
I bought a notebook at the stationery store.
Our house is on top of a hill.
Going up the hill makes me out of breath.
I rode my bike down the hill.

note: Address as 팀장님.

ex.en: Do you have a minute, sir?
I was just promoted to team leader.
Our team leader was late to the meeting.
I ordered car parts.
The repair is delayed because the parts aren't in.
This toy has lots of small parts.
Don't pressure people to drink.
My parents forced me to study.
Nobody forced you.
The key is in my pocket.
I walked with my hands in my pockets.
These pants don't have pockets.
I bought another monitor.
The monitor suddenly turned off.
My eyes hurt if I look at the monitor too long.

note: ㄹ-irregular: 틀어요, 트는, 트세요.

ex.en: Please turn on the AC.
I put on music when I drive.
I turned on the hot water, but nothing's coming out.

note: 첫째, 둘째, 셋째 = first, second, third.

ex.en: I'm on vacation the second week of this month.
I'll sit in the second row.
Our second child is due next month.

note: 해킹당하다 = to get hacked.

ex.en: My account got hacked.
I changed my password because of a hack.

ex.s: 이상한 링크를 누르면 해킹당할 수 있어요.
ex.en: If you click a weird link, you could get hacked.
Don't repeat the same mistake.
I repeated after the teacher.
I keep listening to this song on repeat.
How do I get to the bus terminal?
Please drop me off at Incheon Airport Terminal 2.
I waited for my friend at the terminal.

note: 사정이 있다 = something has come up.

ex.s: 사정이 있어서 못 갈 것 같아요.
ex.en: Something came up, so I don't think I can go.
Things at home have been a bit tough lately.
I explained my situation, and they understood.
I got my lost wallet back.
After a good rest, I got my health back.
I've regained my confidence now.
Hand in your homework by tomorrow.
I submitted the documents online.
I turned in my resignation letter at work.
The payment hasn't gone through yet.
Refunds are processed within three days.
That issue has already been taken care of.
The baby spit up milk.
I threw up from seasickness.
I drank too much yesterday and threw up.
The milk is in the fridge.
Put the leftovers in the fridge.
The fridge broke.

note: Konglish trap: 노트북 = laptop, not notebook (노트).

ex.en: My laptop battery died.
I work on my laptop at cafés.
I'm planning to buy a new laptop.
You should eat protein after working out.
Eggs are high in protein.
These days I drink a protein shake in the morning.

note: 머리 can also mean hair; 머리카락 = the individual hairs.

ex.en: There's a hair in my food.
I'm losing a lot of hair lately.
There's so much hair on the floor.

note: Mostly 애초에 = in the first place, from the start.

ex.en: I shouldn't have gone in the first place.
This wasn't the original plan.
Why did you say that in the first place?

note: 의문이 들다 = to have doubts.

ex.en: I had some doubts about what he said.
My question still hasn't been answered.
It's a mystery why he did that.

note: Used as 정신적으로 or 정신적인. Opposite: 육체적 (physical).

ex.en: I've been really struggling mentally lately.
My friend was a huge emotional support.
Raising kids is very mentally stressful.

note: 개선하다 = to improve something; 개선되다 = to get better.

ex.en: This app needs some improvement.
My health improved after I changed my eating habits.
I heard school lunches have gotten a lot better.

note: 소비하다 = to consume, spend.

ex.en: I've been drinking more coffee lately.
I want to cut down on impulse spending.
I spent way too much this month.

note: For translating texts in general, 번역하다 is more common.

ex.en: How do you interpret this sentence?
There's an app that interprets dreams.
My friend translated the English lyrics for me.

note: Pattern: -다고 가정하다. Unrelated to 가정 = household.

ex.en: Let's plan assuming it rains.
Suppose you had a million won.
We have to assume the worst.

note: 일시 정지 = pause. 정지되다 = to be stopped/suspended.

ex.en: Please pause the video.
The bus stopped suddenly and I almost fell.
My phone service was suspended because I didn't pay.

note: 대량으로 = in bulk.

ex.en: I bought toilet paper in bulk.
Is there a discount if I order in bulk?
We make kimchi in huge batches at kimjang time.

note: Sign: 관계자 외 출입 금지 = staff only.

ex.en: Only staff can go in here.
I asked a staff member at the concert hall.
A school official showed us around.
That movie has a really good screenplay.
My friend is writing a movie script.
We should think about the worst-case scenario too.
